To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the immunoproteomic profile of the hydatid fluid of cystic echincoccosis (Echinococcus granulosis) changes with the progression of the disease.

the immunoproteomic analysis of hydatid fluids from cystic echinoccocis patients revealed that the antigen B-related molecules are the most abundant and the most immunogenic molecules, but that they are not always present and their detection is highly dependent of the stage of the disease.
we identified 40 parasite and 38 host proteins in hydatid fluid from a single fertile cyst, and that the immune recognition of these proteins changed as the disease progressed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunoproteomics of Echinococcous granulosus, and the results may be useful for the development of a diagnostic tool.
the immunoproteomics of E. granulosus HF and the immunodominant molecules of EgAgB, EgAg5, and cathepsins.
the identification of the immunoproteins of HF and their immunological implications for the development of a novel serological test for the diagnosis and monitoring of CE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunodominant antigen of CE is EgAgB1.
the HF immunoproteome is a complex mixture of parasite and host molecules that are differentially recognized by the host immune system according to the disease stages.
immunoproteome profiles of CE are more informative and useful than single molecule-based approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunoproteomic analysis of hydatid cyst fluid could be used as a complementary tool for diagnosis, staging and differential diagnosis of cystic echincococosis.
immunoproteome profiling is an important tool to understand the immunological complexity and to establish a reliable diagnosis for CE.
the immunodominant molecules of E. granulosus metacesode, EgAgB and antigen 5, are highly immunogenic and may serve as potential biomarkers for diagnosis of CE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunoproteomic analysis of the parasite antigenic profile in HF is an important step toward a better understanding of the immunopathological processes of the disease.
the HF proteome of CE2 stage may be more immunogenic and therefore more suitable as a diagnostic reagent.
the immunoproteomic profile of HF may provide an alternative approach for diagnosis and staging of CE.
